cards.observation_text: The lineage report places this animal outside the bovid family.
cards.inference_text: The horned grazer belongs to the excluded branch.
cards.bonus_fact_text: It belongs to the fruit-bat family, a group of large bats native to the Old World.
hints: The family tree turns away from horn-bearing hoofed mammals.

hints.text: The lineage report places it in the big northern mammal branch: hoofed animals, cats, bats, and scaly anteaters.
The lineage keeps its distance from the scale-covered anteater branch.

cards.observation_text: The eyes are visible externally rather than concealed beneath skin.
cards.inference_text: The candidate with skin-covered eyes is incompatible with this finding.
cards.bonus_fact_text: Its body is far smaller than its wingspan, which can reach roughly 1.4 metres.
hints: The front limbs spread wide instead of shoveling forward.

hints.text: The body plan is not a horned, hoofed grazer.
Size estimate: small to medium, light enough for one person to lift.

cards.observation_text: The social record excludes the trunked giant's family herds led by an older female.
cards.inference_text: Other arrangements, including solitary life and different kinds of groups, remain possible.
cards.bonus_fact_text: Groups roost high in montane-forest trees and travel between feeding and roosting sites.
hints: The group gathers above the ground rather than marching across it.

hints.text: It does not roll into an armored ball when threatened.
Group feeding points lack regular planting spacing, and the case has no planting record.

cards.observation_text: The diet record shows this animal is not an ant-and-termite specialist.
cards.inference_text: Cross off the candidate dedicated to those insect colonies.
cards.bonus_fact_text: Fruit and flower feeding helps move seeds and pollen through island forests.
hints: The meal trace comes from plants above ground.

hints.text: It does not hunt large hoofed prey.
Plant food remains cluster at elevated feeding points, supporting an animal seed carrier over wind alone.

cards.observation_text: The mapped range differs from the striped big cat's Asian distribution.
cards.inference_text: That candidate's range is a mismatch; the clue leaves the other range profiles open.
cards.bonus_fact_text: The species survives only on two islands in the Comoros archipelago.
hints: The map pin sits across an ocean from continental Asia.

hints.text: Climate reading: warm tropical conditions all year.
Island range records frame a mapped canopy gap; sampled seedlings trace to parents across that gap.
